To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the task shifting of case management services for HIV/AIDS to CHSCs in urban China is feasible but challenging.

shifting the HIV/AIDS care services from CDCs in urban China to CHSCs may be a feasible option, but there are several challenges in this process, which may compromise its effectiveness and sustainability.

shifting the HIV/AIDS services from Centers for Diseases Control and Prevention ( CDCs) to Community health service Centers (CHSC) is a feasible and necessary approach to cope with growing number of HIV/AIDS cases, but the effectiveness and sustainability may be compromised due to lack of policy and financial support, inadequate human resources, low technical capacity, lack of coordination and fear of discrimination among PLWHA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the task shifting of case management services for HIV/AIDS from CDCs to community health service centers in China.
the policy process of the task shifting approach, and the findings can inform future policy development and practice.
how policy actors can make the most effective use of existing resources to achieve the desired outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

shifting case management services to community health service centers (CHSCs), is feasible, necessary, and should be implemented alongside other efforts, such as increasing public financing and training of health professionals, to make the approach effective and sustainable.
shifting the HIV/AIDS care services to CHSC is a feasible strategy in China but it should be accompanied by other efforts to make it more sustainable.
the HIV/AIDS case managers should be well-trained and equipped with adequate human resources and financial support to provide effective case management services to PLWHA in urban China.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
shifting the case management services to community level is feasible but needs a comprehensive policy and resources support.

the task shifting approach is feasible and necessary, and the policy makers and health managers should take the above-mentioned challenges and enabblers into consideration when implementing such an approach.
shifting the HIV/AIDS services to community level is a feasible and necessary strategy, but there is a need for more research on the sustainability of this shifting approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that

task shifting of HIV/AIDS care from CDCs to community health services is feasible in urban China, but it is necessary to strengthen coordination among different sectors to ensure its effectiveness and sustainability.
policy makers should consider the feasibility and sustainability of the shifting process when they design the policy.
policy makers need to be aware of the potential challenges of task shifting and to develop a feasible and sustainable strategy for the implementation of this approach.
